transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you here and what would you like to talk about?

I guess the main thing is my eating has just… completely gone off the rails. That’s what finally made me think, okay, maybe I shouldn’t keep brushing this off.

I’m usually pretty structured about food, like I track what I eat and I pay attention to meals because it helps me feel like I’m keeping things together. But lately I just stopped caring about any of that. I’d look at the app and just not open it, or I’d think, “I’ll log it later,” and then later never happened. And then it wasn’t even like I was eating badly exactly—it was more like I wasn’t really eating real meals at all. I’d go days where it was mostly coffee and maybe a protein bar here and there, just whatever was easy and didn’t require stopping to think about it.

And the weird part is I didn’t even notice how much it was affecting me until my clothes started feeling loose. Like my pants were hanging differently, shirts weren’t fitting the same, and I remember thinking, “When did that happen?” It sort of scared me because I hadn’t made some intentional plan to lose weight. I just… stopped paying attention to food in this basic way. So that’s why I’m here, I think. It feels like something is really not right with how I’m taking care of myself.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment or interest out of things that you used to like doing?

Yeah. Very much, actually. That’s been one of the stranger parts, because I’m usually someone who has things I go to when I need to feel like myself again.

Like hiking, for example. Normally I’ll look forward to getting out somewhere, even if it’s just a familiar trail, because it clears my head and makes me feel grounded. But lately I just… don’t want to. I’ll think about putting on my boots or driving out there and it feels like too much, or pointless, and then I don’t go.

Same with editing photos. I have folders of shots I took that I’d normally be excited to sort through and work on, and I just keep ignoring them. I open my laptop and then close it again. And even logging meals, which maybe doesn’t sound like a hobby, but it’s part of my routine and usually makes me feel organized — I haven’t even wanted to do that.

There’s also this woodworking project sitting in my garage that I was really into, and I haven’t touched it. Not even to move it around or check on it. It’s just there. And that’s weird for me, because those kinds of things usually keep me steady, like they’re anchors, and lately I just don’t feel interested in any of them.
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time lately, even when things around you haven’t changed much?

Yeah… yes. That’s probably the simplest answer, but it doesn’t feel simple when I try to explain it.

It’s been this heavy, hollow feeling most of the time, like something dropped out from under me. I keep thinking about this moment at work when the sponsor questioned my judgment, and I know people get questioned at work, I know that’s part of the job, but it hit me like… like I’d been exposed as completely incompetent or something. After that I went back to my apartment and just sat there feeling ashamed. Not even angry at first, just empty and embarrassed.

And then I kept opening emails I normally would’ve handled without much thought — routine stuff, things I’m supposed to be able to respond to — and I’d just start crying. Not because the emails were that dramatic, but because they felt like proof that I couldn’t do anything right. It was this awful loop of feeling hollow and then ashamed that I was even reacting that way.

So yes, I’ve felt down and hopeless a lot lately, even when nothing around me was really changing in a way that should explain it. It’s like I can’t get myself back to normal.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling more tired or lacking energy, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean… I don’t think I’ve noticed it in a clear way, like “I’m exhausted all day” or anything that obvious.

It’s more that I’ve been off, and I’m having trouble separating what’s tiredness from what’s just not wanting to do things. Like if I don’t go hiking or don’t work on something in the garage, I can’t tell if that’s because my body has no energy or because I just can’t get myself to care enough to start. Those feel similar from the inside, if that makes sense.

I haven’t been doing a ton physically, so it’s hard to measure. I’m not coming home from some big workout wiped out or anything. I guess I feel slowed down sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it fatigue exactly. More like everything takes more effort than it should, but I’m not sure whether that’s energy or motivation or just… whatever this is.
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual or, on the other hand, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it in a clear, obvious way, like someone saying, “Why are you pacing?” or “Why are you talking so slowly?” Nothing like that has stood out to me.

I mean, there are times where I feel kind of stuck, like I’m sitting there longer than I mean to before I get up or start something, but I don’t know if that’s actually moving slowly or just hesitating. And I wouldn’t say I’m especially fidgety either. I’m not bouncing off the walls or constantly needing to move around, at least not that I’ve really paid attention to.

It’s hard because from the inside, I can tell I’m not quite normal, but I can’t always tell what category it falls into. Like, am I slower physically, or am I just taking longer to make myself do things? I don’t know. I guess I haven’t noticed a major change in my movements either way.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, like not feeling hungry or eating much less than usual, even when you haven’t been trying to lose weight?

Yes. Yeah, definitely. That’s actually one of the reasons I finally thought, okay, something is really not right here, because my eating just kind of… fell apart.

I usually keep pretty close track of what I eat — not in some extreme way, more like it’s part of my routine, especially with work and trying to stay organized — but I just stopped caring. I’d look at the app or think, “I should log this,” and then it was like I couldn’t make myself care enough to do even that tiny thing. And then it wasn’t just the tracking; I stopped eating real meals for stretches of time.

There were days where I was basically living on coffee and protein bars. Like, I’d have coffee in the morning, then realize later I hadn’t eaten anything normal, and instead of making dinner or ordering something decent, I’d just grab a protein bar because it was there and required no thought. It wasn’t that I was trying to lose weight. I wasn’t dieting. I just… food felt like another task, and I didn’t have whatever part of me normally handles that.

And the weird thing is I didn’t even notice the weight part right away. It was more like my clothes started fitting wrong — my pants felt looser, shirts kind of hanging on me differently — and then I was like, wait, how long have I been eating like this? It felt embarrassing, honestly, because I’m usually more on top of basic things like that. But yeah, my appetite and eating have definitely changed.
Have you felt like you have no energy at all, or that even small tasks take a lot of effort lately?

I don’t know if I’d say “no energy at all.” That sounds stronger than what I’m sure of. It’s more like… small tasks feel bigger than they should, but I can’t tell if that’s because I’m actually physically drained or because I’m just not engaging with things the way I normally do.

Like, something simple — getting up to make food, replying to an email, putting something away — it can sit there in my head for way too long before I do it. And from the outside that probably looks like low energy, but from the inside it’s confusing. I’m not always sitting there thinking, “I’m so tired.” Sometimes I’m just stuck, like there’s this extra layer between deciding to do something and actually doing it.

So… yes, small things have felt harder lately, but I’m not sure I’d describe it as having no energy. It’s more like everything takes more effort, and I don’t really know what bucket to put that in.
Have you felt depressed or had a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yeah. I mean… yes, I think that’s probably the most accurate way to say it. It hasn’t just been like having a bad afternoon or being stressed from work. It’s been this heavy, low feeling that sort of takes over the whole day.

The thing that really sticks in my mind is after the sponsor questioned my judgment. I know, logically, people get questioned at work all the time, and normally I can handle that. I can write the email, clarify the decision, explain the tradeoffs, whatever. That’s basically part of my job. But this time it was like the bottom just dropped out from under me. I went home and sat in my apartment feeling completely hollow and ashamed, like I had failed in some huge, personal way.

And I was crying over emails. Like actual emails that, on a normal day, I would have just dealt with. I’d open one, read it, and it would feel unbearable, like every sentence was proof that I couldn’t do anything right. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but that’s what it felt like. I wasn’t just annoyed or embarrassed. I felt low and empty for most of the day, and it kept happening, not just once and then gone.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hiking or working on projects, no longer feel rewarding or pleasurable to you?

Yeah… yes. That’s actually been one of the stranger parts, because it’s not just that I’m too busy or that I haven’t had time. It’s like the things that usually make me feel like myself just don’t have the same pull anymore.

Hiking is a big one. Normally, even if work is a mess, I can get out somewhere for a few hours and it kind of resets me. Even just planning a route or checking the weather would usually make me feel a little better. Lately I’ll think, “I should go,” and then there’s just nothing behind it. No anticipation, no feeling of, yeah, that would be good. It feels like another item on a list.

Same with editing photos. I have folders sitting there that I would normally be excited to go through, and I just… don’t want to open them. And logging meals, too — that’s not exactly “fun,” I guess, but it used to be part of feeling organized and grounded, like I was keeping some structure. I haven’t even wanted to do that.

And the woodworking project in my garage — that one bothers me because I usually really like having something physical to work on, something where I can see progress. But I haven’t even touched it. I’ll walk past it and think, “I should at least sand that piece,” or “I should clean up the bench,” and then I just keep walking. It’s strange, because those things usually keep me grounded, and now they feel kind of flat or unreachable.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up a lot during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely been off. It’s not even just one clean thing like, “I can’t fall asleep,” or “I’m sleeping too much.” It’s more like… even when I do try to sleep, it doesn’t feel like I’m really getting away from anything.

I’ll go to bed and think I’m done for the night, but then I keep waking up at these weird hours — like not a normal “roll over and go back to sleep” kind of waking up. I’ll come fully awake and my mind is already back in the deployment plan, like I’m mentally checking timelines or replaying what needs to happen or what I might have missed. It’s frustrating because I’m lying there in the dark, knowing I should be resting, and instead it’s like my brain has reopened the whole thing.

And then by morning I don’t feel rested. I feel wrecked. Like I technically spent time in bed, but it doesn’t feel like it counted. It makes the next day harder because I start out already worn down, and then the same stuff is waiting for me again.
